summary: Reynolds County, MO 85-foot steel tower on the former Deer Run State Park, now in Current River Conservation Area; register dates it 1926; MDC lists it as standing.

staffing.status: towerman named in 1951; no later staffing record found

access.note: On Current River Conservation Area, a public MDC area, and listed by MDC as a place of interest; no closure notice found, but whether the cab is open to climbing is not confirmed

visit.trail_note: The self-guided elk driving tour route passes the fire tower; ask MDC about climbing before going up

events.note: Build year as stated by the NHLR 'Built' field; no source given there, and the earliest press item found (1930) gives no build date
June 25, 1930 newspaper item describes a fire tower built to protect game and new pine growth
Towersite development: a dwelling, garage and woodshed, latrine and cistern
Clarence Pratt named as towerman at Deer Run in a newspaper item
Extra bedroom added to the tower residence (FY1956-57)
Coast and Geodetic Survey station description gives the tower's overall height as about 100 feet
MDC combined four smaller areas into the Current River Conservation Area, which now includes the tower
Registered December 12, 2013; nominated by Jim Lyon

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 1926 without a source; the earliest press item found (June 1930) describes a built tower without a date. The story keeps 1926 as the register's stated year and marks it unconfirmed.
The register and the 1939-41 state report say 85 feet; a 1962 survey note says about 100 feet. The record uses 85 feet (25.9 m) as the stated height and the story reports the disagreement.
Names vary: the register says Deer Run State Park, a 1947-48 state manual says Deer Run State Forest, and River Hills lists both plus Deer Run Refuge and Conservation Area.

notes_for_editor: Build year 1926 is the register's figure with no source; the 1930 press item is the earliest found. Height disagrees (85 ft vs about 100 ft in 1962). Climbing status is unconfirmed: the Semissourian and Missouri Life articles returned 403 and were not read, so the access level is public area, climbing unknown. Staffing record stops at 1951. About 6 page reads used.
